verdict.label: not_comparable
verdict.rationale: The two claims address different exposure–outcome pairs. Study A (PMID 27299816) reports that serum resistin levels correlated with fat mass and other body-composition indicators of fat accretion in children and adolescents (sentences 11–12). Study B (PMID 34169498) reports that in T2DM patients resistin was not associated with BMI (sentence 9). Even if fat accretion and BMI were treated as related adiposity measures, the exposures are not aligned: A treats fat mass as the exposure and resistin as the outcome, whereas B treats resistin as the exposure and BMI as the outcome, and the populations (children/adolescents vs. adults with type 2 diabetes) differ. No comparable exposure–outcome contrast is available from the abstracts.

source_evidence.quote: In the whole sample and among obese subjects, resistin levels correlated with body mass index, tricipital skinfold, arm circumference, arm fat area and fat mass.
In conclusion, in contrast to leptin and adiponectin, in T2DM patients, resistin is not associated with BMI and IR, but with inflammation and worse kidney function.

diagnostics.notes: Extraction on both sides is faithful to the sources: A's claim (exposure fat mass, outcome serum resistin, correlation) matches sentence 11; B's claim (resistin not associated with BMI) matches sentence 9. The obstacle is comparability, not extraction: different exposure–outcome pairs (fat mass → resistin vs. resistin → BMI), different populations (children/adolescents vs. T2DM adults), and no shared contrast. Note also that A reports a positive resistin–BMI correlation, which does not rescue comparability with B's explicit resistin–BMI null because the selected claims themselves are not aligned.
